thread.title: Tech Today: Qualcomm LBO? Micron Options Plays, Apple’s Next A.R.

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Qualcomm LBO? Micron Options Plays, Apple’s Next A.R.
text:
Apple's bringing its augmented reality sensors to more models of the iPhone later this year, according to a report from analyst Jun Zhang of the boutique research house Rosenblatt Securities / Credit: Tiernan Ray for Barron's. Here are some things going on today in your world of tech :
Here comes Zscaler The Nasdaq is awaiting a new tech offering this morning, eleven-year-old Zscaler of San Jose, which is to start trading under the ticker “ ZS .” The deal priced at $16, above an expected range of $13 to $15, and is indicated to open at $26.
For more on ZScaler, see the S1 prospectus .
Broadcom fizzles Shares of chip giant Broadcom ( AVGO ) are down $10.42, or almost 4%, at $257.34, despite the company yesterday afternoon reporting fiscal Q1 results that topped analysts' expectations, and offering a higher revenue forecast for this quarter.
CFO Thomas Krause on a conference call with analysts said that he and CEO Hock Tan see potential M&A targets, and would not be held back despite the fact the company had to walk away this week from its hostile bid for Qualcomm ( QCOM ).
There are no ratings changes, that I can see, but price targets are going higher as estimates go higher at many shops.
Canaccord Genuity’s Mike Walkley notes the company plans to return half its free cash flow to investors, and he reiterates his Buy rating, and raises his price target to $340 from $325, writing that “given the strong business model and anticipated FCF generation, we anticipate material dividend increases after the F18 and F19 fiscal years."
With the wireless end market being “choppy,” however, Kinngai Chan of Summit Insights Group this morning writes that "We expect AVGO's organic financial outperformance to moderate further into 2018,” adding that "AVGO will need to pursue large acquisitions in order to achieve meaningful future earnings outperformance."
Qualcomm LBO? Meantime, while Broadcom fizzles, shares of Qualcomm are up $1.10, or 1.8%, at $60.99, a the Street this parses the bizarre rumor overnight , from The Financial Times , that Qualcomm’s former chairman, Paul Jacobs , is interested in taking the company private and has been talking with large investors, including SoftBank ( 9984JP ), about buying out Qualcomm.
CNBC ’s David Faber this morning related that unnamed sources told him Jacobs sent a letter Tuesday about the idea to the board, and has mentioned the idea before, and noted that more than one “source close to the board” told him “ they think [Jacobs] has snapped ” and is “ not acting rationally ."
Faber argues that a price that would be acceptable to Qualcomm investors, perhaps $87 per share, would require a $130 billion in total, perhaps $30 billion in equity, and would therefore be “virtually impossible” and “this is not going to happen."
Adobe shines Shares of Adobe Systems ( ADBE ) are up $6.39, or 3%, at $225.26, continuing last night’s after hours gains following the company’s better-than-expected fiscal Q1 report and higher forecast for this quarter.
Price targets are zooming into the $250 to $260 price range at numerous shops. Cowen & Co .’s J. Derrick Wood , reiterating his Outperform rating on the shares, raises his target to $255 from $220, calling the report “fantastic."
"Digital Media remains the main upside driver as the various growth vectors are hitting on all cylinders,” he writes. "With mgmt indicating that price increases will have even greater effect next year, there seems to be very good durability of growth/margin strength ahead."
Micron options Speaking of chips, another day, another favorable review for Micron Technology ( MU ) in advance of its earnings report next Thursday, March 22nd, after the closing bell
Tristan Gerra with R.W. Baird reiterates an Outperform rating on the stock, and raises his price target to $100 from $60, writing "In DRAM , we expect a significant increase in contract pricing in C1H18, while NAND flash C1H pricing reductions are more muted than previously expected."
Also today, J.P. Morgan ’s Shawn Quigg offers an options strategy for Micron: "overlaying stock positions with May 65/70/75 call trees (i.e. buy one 65 strike call, sell one 70 and one 75 strike call) for a net credit of $0.02, indicatively ($58.84 reference price)."
Micron shares are up $1.09, or 1.8%, at $59.93.
Apple’s A.R. plans Rosenblatt ’s Jun Zhang this morning relates that his supply-chain sources tell him Apple ( AAPL ) will have more iPhones with augmented reality this fall, including a 6.1-inch model with an LCD screen and a single rear camera with a 3-D sensing design; a larger 6.5-inch OLED model, and an iPad Pro with augmented reality.
Zhang warns that Q2 production for iPhone is being reduced, and so things could be tough for suppliers Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ), Knowles ( KN ), Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ), Qorvo ( QRVO ), and Universal Display ( OLED ).
Apple shares today are down 22 cents at $178.43, while shares of suppliers are all going higher, with Cirrus up $1.41, or 3%, at $44.47, and Universal Display up 50 cents, or 0.4%, at $124.05.
Tesla under the gun Amidst speculation of production problems with faulty builds at Tesla Motors ( TSLA ), The Wall Street Journal ’s Tim Higgins and Susan Pulliam today offer a piece about CEO Elon Musk being under pressure to hit a goal of producing 5,000 units per week of its new Model 3 sedan by the end of June, a goal it has twice delayed.
Tesla shares today are down $5.18, or 1.5%, at $320.42.
